sample_unit: practices submitting at least one survey response (survey sent to 263 general practitioners and assistants)
models_evaluated: Pacmed ML-based CDSS for urinary tract infection treatment

links.outcome: User-reported workflow integration, usability and acceptance of the CDSS after a 4-month implementation
links.effect: 48% found the software easy to integrate into workflow; 67% trusted output; 52% agreed it supported decisions; 9% of practices dropped out in first 8 weeks; assistants under-involved in design.
links.quote: Forty-eight percent of respondents found the software easy to integrate into their clinical workflow.

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating the usability, usefulness, and adoption of an ML-based clinical decision support system deployed in real primary care practices for UTI treatment.
